bibl.title: Brain function in coma, vegetative state, and related disorders

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Moreover, in the VS patients, the activated primary somatosensory cortex was shown to exist as an island, functionally disconnected from higher-order associative cortices of the pain-matrix.

span.label: disorders of consciousness after severe brain damage
span.quote: We review the nosological criteria and functional neuroanatomical basis for brain death, coma, vegetative state, minimally conscious state and the locked-in state.

span.label: review
span.quote: References were selected on the basis of relevance and accessibility.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: progressive Wallerian and transsynaptic neuronal degeneration drives the further fall of brain metabolism as a vegetative state becomes permanent
span.quote: This progressive loss of metabolic functioning over time is the result of progressive Wallerian and transsynaptic neuronal degeneration.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: sparing of brainstem structures (pedunculopontine reticular formation, hypothalamus, basal forebrain) preserves arousal and autonomic function while the cortex is impaired, producing wakeful unawareness
span.quote: Characteristic of VS patients is a relative sparing of metabolism in the brainstem (encompassing the pedunculopontine reticular formation, the hypothalamus and the basal forebrain).62 The functional preservation of these structures allows for the preserved arousal and autonomic functions in these patients.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: functional disconnection of primary sensory cortex from multimodal and limbic areas stops residual cortical processing from reaching the integrative stage held to be necessary for awareness
span.quote: Moreover, a cascade of functional disconnections were observed along the auditory cortical pathways, from primary auditory areas to multimodal and limbic areas,70 suggesting that the observed residual cortical processing in the VS does not lead to integrative processes which are thought to be necessary for awareness.

span.label: The imaging methods reviewed are hard to apply and interpret in this patient population.
span.note: what this limits: this patient population specifically: USE OF THESE TECHNIQUES IN SEVERELY BRAIN-DAMAGED PERSONS IS METHODOLOGICALLY COMPLEX AND REQUIRES CAREFUL QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION
span.quote: However, use of these techniques in severely brain-damaged persons is methodologically complex and requires careful quantitative analysis and interpretation.

span.label: PET metabolic measures cannot yet be linked to patient outcome.
span.note: what this limits: any prognostic use of PET metabolism: AT PRESENT, THERE IS NO ESTABLISHED CORRELATION BETWEEN CEREBRAL METABOLIC RATES OF GLUCOSE OR OXYGEN AS MEASURED BY PET AND PATIENT OUTCOME
span.quote: At present, there is no established correlation between cerebral metabolic rates of glucose or oxygen as measured by PET and patient outcome.

span.label: The minimally conscious state has almost no imaging evidence base yet.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about the minimally conscious state: BECAUSE CRITERIA FOR THE MCS HAVE ONLY RECENTLY BEEN INTRODUCED, THERE ARE VERY FEW FUNCTIONAL IMAGING STUDIES OF PATIENTS IN THIS CONDITION
span.quote: Because criteria for the MCS have only recently been introduced, there are very few functional imaging studies of patients in this condition.

span.label: The central construct has no objective measure; its estimation is stated to require interpretation of clinical signs.
span.note: what this limits: any consciousness determination in these patients as an objective measurement: the review states it cannot be measured by any machine and requires interpretation of clinical signs
span.quote: Unfortunately, for the time being, consciousness cannot be measured objectively by any machine. Its estimation requires the interpretation of several clinical signs.

span.label: The criteria for brain death are stated to differ between countries, some requiring brainstem death only and others whole-brain death.
span.note: what this limits: a brain-death determination as a jurisdiction-independent fact: the review states the diagnostic criteria differ from country to country
span.quote: the diagnostic criteria differ from country to country.15 Some rely on the death of the brainstem only,16 others require death of the whole brain including the brain stem.

span.label: Diagnosis rests on inference from responses observed at the moment of examination, and misdiagnosis of these states is stated to be frequent.
span.note: what this limits: a recorded diagnosis of VS, MCS or locked-in syndrome as settled: the review states misdiagnosis is frequent and assessment infers from responses at the time of examination
span.quote: This difficulty is reflected in the frequent misdiagnoses of VS, MCS and locked-in syndrome (LIS).1-7 Bedside evaluation of residual brain function in severely brain-damaged patients is difficult because motor responses may be very limited or inconsistent. In addition, consciousness is not an all-or-none phenomenon8 and its clinical assessment relies on inferences made from observed responses to external stimuli at the time of the examination.

span.label: The three sources of uncertainty are stated together in one sentence and compound each other: motor responses may be limited or inconsistent, consciousness is not all-or-none, and the assessment is an inference from responses observed at the moment of examination.
span.quote: In addition, consciousness is not an all-or-none phenomenon8 and its clinical assessment relies on inferences made from observed responses to external stimuli at the time of the examination

span.label: studies whose clinical detail was too thin to guarantee the accuracy of the diagnosis were excluded from the review
span.note: eliminates: that the review's conclusions rest on cases whose diagnostic category - coma, vegetative state, minimally conscious - cannot be trusted
span.quote: We excluded certain studies in which clinical details provided were insufficient to guarantee accuracy of diagnoses.

span.label: brain death
span.quote: Most countries have published recommendations for the diagnosis of brain death but the diagnostic criteria differ from country to country.15 Some rely on the death of the brainstem only,16 others require death of the whole brain including the brain stem.

span.label: minimally conscious state
span.quote: The emergence of MCS is defined by the ability to use functional interactive communication or functional use of objects.

span.label: consciousness
span.quote: Unfortunately, for the time being, consciousness cannot be measured objectively by any machine. Its estimation requires the interpretation of several clinical signs.

span.label: consciousness - defined here for assessability rather than for correctness: as it can be assessed at the patient's bedside
span.quote: In the present review, we will first define consciousness as it can be assessed at the patient’s bedside.

span.label: consciousness - explicitly not an all-or-none phenomenon, which is why bedside assessment is difficult
span.quote: consciousness is not an all-or-none phenomenon

span.label: emergence from the minimally conscious state - defined by a capability: functional interactive communication or functional use of objects
span.quote: The emergence of MCS is defined by the ability to use functional interactive communication or functional use of objects.

span.label: brain death - a category whose criteria are jurisdictional: brainstem death in some countries, whole-brain death in others, with the concept itself 'largely accepted' either way
span.quote: Most countries have published recommendations for the diagnosis of brain death but the diagnostic criteria differ from country to country.15 Some rely on the death of the brainstem only,16 others require death of the whole brain

span.label: qualifies → the irreversible-neuronal-loss reading (ref. 64)
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE SAME METABOLIC IMPAIRMENT IS DAMAGE OR DYSFUNCTION - and the review states the disagreement rather than settling it: 'IT IS STILL CONTROVERSIAL whether the observed metabolic impairment in this large cortical network reflects an IRREVERSIBLE STRUCTURAL NEURONAL LOSS, OR FUNCTIONAL AND POTENTIALLY REVERSIBLE DAMAGE.' The evidence offered against the first reading is a rare case class, not a test: 'HOWEVER, IN THE RARE CASES WHERE VS PATIENTS RECOVER awareness ... PET SHOWS A FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY of metabolism in these same cortical regions'
span.quote: It is still controversial whether 8 the observed metabolic impairment in this large cortical network reflects an irreversible structural neuronal loss,64 or functional and potentially reversible damage. However, in the rare cases where VS patients recover awareness of self and environment, PET shows a functional recovery of metabolism in these same cortical regions.

span.label: builds-on → Andrews et al. 1996, Childs et al. 1993 and five others (refs. 1-7)
span.note: differs in: WHAT THE MISDIAGNOSIS RATE IS EVIDENCE OF. The review cites seven misdiagnosis studies not as a finding about clinicians but as evidence that THE CATEGORY IS HARD TO APPLY AT THE BEDSIDE, and gives two reasons in the same passage: 'motor responses may be very limited or inconsistent', and 'CONSCIOUSNESS IS NOT AN ALL-OR-NONE PHENOMENON and its clinical assessment relies on INFERENCES MADE FROM OBSERVED RESPONSES to external stimuli AT THE TIME OF THE EXAMINATION'
span.quote: This difficulty is reflected in the frequent misdiagnoses of VS, MCS and locked-in syndrome (LIS).1-7 Bedside evaluation of residual brain function in severely brain-damaged patients is difficult because motor responses may be very limited or inconsistent. In addition, consciousness is not an all-or-none phenomenon8 and its clinical assessment relies on inferences made from observed responses to external stimuli at the time of the examination.

span.label: brain death —operationalised-as→ consciousness
span.note: differs in: THE JURISDICTION. The criteria for the same category 'DIFFER FROM COUNTRY TO COUNTRY' - some require death of the brainstem only, others death of the whole brain. Whether a given patient is dead by this definition depends on where the examination happens · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The paper reports the variation as a fact about the literature, not as a criticism: 'The concept of brain death as defining the death of the individual is largely accepted' AND the criteria differ. AGREEMENT ON THE CATEGORY, DISAGREEMENT ON ITS BOUNDARY, stated in consecutive sentences.
span.quote: Most countries have published recommendations for the diagnosis of brain death but the diagnostic criteria differ from country to country.15 Some rely on the death of the brainstem only,16 others require death of the whole brain including the brain stem.17 However, the clinical assessments for brain death are very uniform and based on the loss of all brainstem reflexes and the demonstration of continuing apnoea in a persistently comatose patient.18 Coma Coma is characterized by the absence of arousal and thus also of consciousness.

span.label: consciousness —operationalised-as→ minimally conscious state
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE MEASUREMENT IS AN INFERENCE FROM A MOMENT: assessment 'relies on INFERENCES made from OBSERVED RESPONSES to external stimuli AT THE TIME OF THE EXAMINATION' - and in the same sentence the paper says consciousness 'is NOT an all-or-none phenomenon'. A graded thing, assessed by a snapshot, in patients whose motor responses 'may be very limited or inconsistent'. The record already carries both readings as senses.
span.quote: In addition, consciousness is not an all-or-none phenomenon8 and its clinical assessment relies on inferences made from observed responses to external stimuli at the time of the examination

span.label: The metabolic hallmark of the vegetative state is impaired metabolism in the polymodal associative cortices - bilateral prefrontal regions, Broca's area, parieto-temporal and posterior parietal areas, and precuneus.
span.quote: The other hallmark of the vegetative state is a systematic impairment of metabolism in the polymodal associative cortices (bilateral prefrontal regions, Broca’s area, parieto-temporal and posterior parietal areas and precuneus).

span.label: Intense noxious stimulation reached midbrain, contralateral thalamus and primary somatosensory cortex in every one of 15 vegetative patients, so primary sensory cortex remains reachable even when cortical evoked potentials are absent.
span.quote: High intensity noxious electrical stimulation activated midbrain, contralateral thalamus and primary somatosensory cortex in each and every one of the 15 vegetative patients studied, even in the absence of detectable cortical evoked potentials.

span.label: The same noxious stimulation failed to activate secondary somatosensory, insular, posterior parietal and anterior cingulate cortices in any vegetative patient, although all of these were activated in every control subject.
span.quote: However, secondary somatosensory, insular, posterior parietal and anterior cingulate cortices, which were activated in all control subjects, failed to show significant activation in a single vegetative patient

span.label: The medial parietal cortex (precuneus) and the adjacent posterior cingulate cortex are the regions whose metabolism separates minimally conscious from vegetative patients.
span.quote: The medial parietal cortex (precuneus) and adjacent posterior cingulate cortex seem to be brain regions that differentiate minimally conscious from vegetative patients.

span.label: Patients in the locked-in state show significantly higher brain metabolic levels than vegetative patients on PET, matching their intact awareness.
span.quote: PET scanning has shown significantly higher metabolic levels in the brains of patients in a LIS compared to patients in the VS.

span.label: The lumped constant used to compute glucose metabolism from FDG-PET is not stable in damaged brains: it falls globally after traumatic brain injury and rises regionally in severe cerebral ischaemia, so absolute metabolic rates in these patients are unreliable.
span.quote: However, in traumatic brain injury, a significant global decrease in lumped constant has recently been reported94 and in severe cerebral ischaemia, regional lumped constant values are

span.label: Despite the promise of functional neuroimaging, clinical examination and the nosological categories it establishes remain the standard for diagnosis and prognosis in these patients.
span.quote: At present, nosological distinctions confirmed by clinical examinations remain the standard for accurate diagnosis and prognosis.

span.label: consciousness (level vs content)
span.quote: Consciousness is a multifaceted concept that can be divided into two major components: the level of consciousness (i.e., arousal, wakefulness or vigilance) and the content of consciousness (i.e., awareness of the environment and of the self)

span.label: coma
span.quote: Coma is characterized by the absence of arousal and thus also of consciousness. It is a state of unarousable unresponsiveness in which the patient lies with the eyes closed and has no awareness of self and surroundings.

span.label: persistent vegetative state
span.quote: “Persistent VS” has been arbitrarily defined as a vegetative state still present one month after acute traumatic or non-traumatic brain damage but does not imply irreversibility.

span.label: minimally conscious state (MCS)
span.quote: To be considered as minimally conscious, patients have to show limited but clearly discernible evidence of consciousness of self or environment, on a reproducible or sustained basis, by at least one of the following behaviours: (1) following simple commands, (2) gestural or verbal yes/no response (regardless of accuracy), (3) intelligible verbalization, (4) purposeful behaviour

span.label: locked-in syndrome
span.quote: The term "locked-in" syndrome was introduced by Plum and Posner in 1966 to reflect the quadriplegia and anarthria brought about by the disruption of corticospinal and corticobulbar pathways, respectively.

span.label: hollow skull phenomenon
span.quote: Functional imaging using cerebral perfusion tracers and single photon emission computed tomography29-34 or cerebral metabolism tracers and PET 35 typically show an “hollow skull phenomenon” in brain death patients, confirming the absence of neuronal function in the whole brain

span.label: 40-50% — overall cortical metabolism of vegetative patients as a proportion of normal values
span.quote: Overall cortical metabolism of vegetative patients is 40-50% of normal values.

span.label: 30-40% — brain metabolism in permanent vegetative state (12 months after trauma, 3 months after non-traumatic damage) as a proportion of normal values
span.quote: In “permanent” VS (i.e., 12 months after a trauma or 3 months following a non-traumatic brain damage), brain metabolism values drop to 30-40% of normal values.

span.label: 28% — lowest reported brain metabolism, measured under propofol anaesthesia, as a proportion of normal values
span.quote: The lowest values of brain metabolism have been reported during propofol anesthesia (28% of normal values).

span.label: 40% — cortical cerebral metabolism during deep sleep (stages III-IV) as a proportion of normal values
span.quote: In this daily physiological condition cortical cerebral metabolism can drop to nearly 40% of normal values

span.label: 75% — cerebral metabolic rate for glucose, as a proportion of normal, in patients who recover from postanoxic coma
span.quote: In patients who recover from a postanoxic coma, cerebral metabolic rates for glucose are 75% of normal values.

span.label: 15 — number of vegetative patients in whom noxious electrical stimulation activated midbrain, thalamus and primary somatosensory cortex
span.quote: High intensity noxious electrical stimulation activated midbrain, contralateral thalamus and primary somatosensory cortex in each and every one of the 15 vegetative patients studied, even in the absence of detectable cortical evoked potentials.
